findings.claim: BYPASS_RULE_ID is written to GITHUB_ENV using a bare printf KEY=VALUE\n pattern without stripping newlines. A crafted rule_id containing an embedded newline can inject additional KEY=VALUE pairs into the runner environment for all subsequent steps, including SCP_THRESHOLD=allow, which disables all threshold enforcement regardless of the bypass scope.
findings.evidence: policy-check.yml lines 295-298: `printf 'SCP_BYPASS_RULE_ID=%s\n' "${BYPASS_RULE_ID}" >> "${GITHUB_ENV}"`. GitHub Actions GITHUB_ENV format: each line is parsed as KEY=VALUE; a newline within the value terminates the current assignment and begins a new one. BYPASS_RULE_ID is set by bash command substitution from policy-findings.json (lines 237-251); bash command substitution strips only TRAILING newlines, preserving embedded ones. If a deny finding's rule_id is 'SCP-R-001\nSCP_THRESHOLD=allow', BYPASS_RULE_ID carries the embedded newline. The verify-bypass-pairing.sh jq query uses --arg rule_id which handles newlines in the string correctly, so gate 2 passes if a matching waiver with the same newline-containing rule_id is in the diff. All three gates can pass with a crafted newline-containing rule_id paired with a matching waiver. Lines 295-298 then write: SCP_BYPASS_RULE_ID=SCP-R-001 (first line, truncated) and SCP_THRESHOLD=allow (second line, injected). The threshold enforcement step reads os.environ.get('SCP_THRESHOLD') == 'deny' at line 362; with SCP_THRESHOLD='allow', sys.exit(1) is never called. All effective_denies are silently suppressed for this run. The same injection vector can forge SCP_BYPASS_DECISION_ID (line 297), SCP_BYPASS_EXPIRES_AT (line 298), and any other downstream-consumed env var.
findings.impact: An attacker who controls the policy evaluation output (020C Rego scope) can craft a finding with a newline-bearing rule_id, commit a matching waiver in a PR, and wait for a repo maintainer to activate scp_bypass=true. When all three gates pass, GITHUB_ENV injection suppresses the threshold check for ALL deny findings — not just the approved rule — turning the break-glass primitive into a full policy enforcement bypass. The attack requires 020C compromise plus human activation of break-glass, but the vulnerability is present in the 020B code that will be live when 020C ships and cannot be patched without a 020B file change. Additionally, the 020B scaffold already writes SCP_BYPASS_DECISION_ID and SCP_BYPASS_EXPIRES_AT via the same pattern, extending the injection surface to those fields.
findings.mitigation:
Before the printf writes at lines 295-298, validate BYPASS_RULE_ID contains only safe characters: `if ! printf '%s' "${BYPASS_RULE_ID}" | grep -qE '^[A-Za-z0-9_.:/-]+$'; then emit_error "SCP-E004" "${SCP_WAIVERS_PATH}" "BYPASS_RULE_ID contains characters invalid for a rule identifier"; exit 1; fi`. This check belongs immediately after the empty-string guard at line 253 so it applies before the script is called. Alternatively, use the GITHUB_ENV multiline EOF delimiter format for all four writes: `printf 'SCP_BYPASS_RULE_ID<<EOF
%s
EOF
' "${BYPASS_RULE_ID}" >> "${GITHUB_ENV}"` — but note this changes the value seen by consumers (trailing newline added) so the threshold step's string comparison must be updated. The allowlist-regex approach is simpler and matches the governance invariant that rule_ids follow a structured naming convention (SCP-R-NNN, etc.).

The bypass gate never writes to output/findings/waivers-applied.json, so the waivers_applied array in the artifact is always empty even during an active bypass. Machine consumers of the artifact (WP-SCP-023 aggregators) cannot identify the bypassed rule from the artifact alone.

findings.evidence: verify-bypass-pairing.sh lines 78-88: `if 'T' in raw: ... valid = expiry > datetime.now(timezone.utc)` (datetime path is UTC-correct); `else: expiry = date.fromisoformat(raw); valid = expiry > date.today()` (date-only path uses local timezone). date.today() returns the local date, not UTC. If the runner is configured as UTC-12 and the UTC date is 2026-05-15, date.today() returns 2026-05-14. A waiver with expires_at='2026-05-14' satisfies `2026-05-14 > 2026-05-14` = False (correctly rejected). But a waiver with expires_at='2026-05-15' satisfies `2026-05-15 > 2026-05-14` = True even though UTC date is already 2026-05-15 (accepted 24h past intended expiry in the worst case). GitHub-hosted ubuntu-24.04 runners use UTC by default; the vulnerability only manifests on self-hosted runners with non-UTC configuration.
findings.impact: A waiver that has expired by UTC time may continue to satisfy the bypass gate for up to 24 hours on self-hosted runners with a UTC-negative timezone. The core time-boundary governance control (waivers are time-limited) is weakened. Risk is bounded by the timezone offset (maximum 12 hours in practice) and limited to self-hosted runner configurations, which are non-default for this workflow. The datetime-path (ISO 8601 with T) is correctly UTC-normalised; only the date-only path is affected.
findings.mitigation: Replace `date.today()` with a UTC-normalised equivalent: `from datetime import date, datetime, timezone; utc_today = datetime.now(timezone.utc).date(); valid = expiry > utc_today`. This one-line change makes date-only expiry consistent with the datetime-path UTC handling and removes the timezone dependency. Update the Python block at lines 83-84 in verify-bypass-pairing.sh.

findings.claim: Dead code at workflow lines 262-265 (waivers-path existence check after the script invocation) was flagged as C-nit-02 in the R1 consolidation and remains unaddressed after fix-round-1. The verify-bypass-pairing.sh script already exits non-zero when the waivers file does not exist (line 39 of the script), so the outer check is never reached.
findings.evidence: policy-check.yml lines 257-260: script is called; on non-zero exit, emit_error SCP-E004 fires and the step exits 1. Lines 262-265: `if [ ! -f "${SCP_WAIVERS_PATH}" ]; then emit_error SCP-E004 ...; exit 1; fi` — this block is only reachable if the script returned 0, but the script exits 1 when the file is absent (verify-bypass-pairing.sh line 39). verify-bypass-pairing.sh line 39: `if [ ! -f "${waivers_path}" ]; then echo ... >&2; exit 1; fi`. The outer check was noted as C-nit-02 in consolidation-r1.json and MIN/nit findings are not required closes in the fix-round, so this is expected-open.
findings.impact: No runtime impact. Dead code adds noise and could mislead a reader into believing the outer check provides meaningful defense-in-depth. The waivers-path guard is solely inside the script.
findings.mitigation: Remove lines 262-265 from the bypass gate step, leaving the script as the sole existence guard. This reduces dead code and makes the step's control flow easier to audit.

self_reported_concerns: MAJ-R2-BYPASS-001 (GITHUB_ENV newline injection) requires 020C policy evaluation to be compromised AND a human maintainer to activate break-glass with a PR that contains an obviously malformed rule_id containing a newline. The attack surface is narrow but the resulting suppression of ALL threshold enforcement (not just the approved rule) makes the impact disproportionate to the preconditions. The fix (allowlist-regex on BYPASS_RULE_ID) is one line and should be included in the next fix round regardless.

MAJ-R2-BYPASS-002 (bypass_emitted without rule_id) is a structural gap in the audit trail. It cannot be compensated by workflow log correlation at scale. The fix requires schema changes (additionalProperties: false must be opened) and summary builder changes. This is in-scope for 020B files.

The waivers-file.schema.json requires created_at for both entry shapes (lines 14 and 54). The R1 mitigation text listed created_at as optional for the rule-bypass shape. Current implementation is STRICTER than the mitigation required, which is safe but may surprise operators who attempt to add a bypass waiver without created_at. No security gap — schema validation in gate 3 would reject such an entry. Noted as an operational friction point.

CRIT-BYPASS-001 residual: Conftest still lacks Sigstore attestation (gh attestation verify) while OPA has it. Both binaries now require SHA256 verification before execution. The comment at line 158 acknowledges the gap. This is a residual supply-chain risk, not a regression from fix-round-1, and does not constitute a new CRIT or MAJ at R2.
structured_review.summary: Fix-round-1 closed all five targeted R1 safety findings: the unverified Conftest bare-binary fallback is gone, expires_at is validated against today in verify-bypass-pairing.sh, the D-NNN decision-row grep now chains grep -F to require the rule_id substring, the waivers diff-membership check is rewritten with jq --arg (injection-safe), and SCP_BYPASS_APPROVED is correctly written to GITHUB_ENV with effective_denies filtering limited to the approved rule. CG-CRIT-01 (gate-2/gate-3 incompatibility) is also resolved: waivers-file.schema.json now accepts rule-bypass entries. Fresh R2 attack of the resulting code reveals two new MAJ and two nit findings. MAJ-R2-BYPASS-001: BYPASS_RULE_ID is written to GITHUB_ENV using simple KEY=VALUE printf without newline sanitization; a crafted rule_id containing an embedded newline can inject arbitrary env vars — in particular SCP_THRESHOLD=allow — into subsequent workflow steps, suppressing all threshold enforcement when break-glass is active. MAJ-R2-BYPASS-002: the summary artifact records bypass_emitted:true but omits the bypassed rule_id, expires_at, and decision_id; the bypass gate never writes to output/findings/waivers-applied.json, so WP-SCP-023 machine consumers cannot identify which rule was bypassed from the artifact alone. Both MAJ findings require fix before merge.
